producers.note: No OBR estimate of the household cost, poverty effect or support-policy costs. The Fiscal risks and sustainability report (July 2026) names the conflict as a risk without a household estimate; the forecast evaluation report (June 2026) returned 403 and was not read. The OBR's only war-specific figure seen is David Miles's 10 March 2026 evidence (prices about 1 per cent higher by end-2026), quoted on the dashboard, not read at its source. The dashboard sets it beside its CPI additions, which are scenario parameters (parameters.registry: the Summer 2026 prices value is the Bank of England's June 2026 projection of about 1 point, raised to the 1.28 point first-round effect of the scenario's own prices; the two escalation values are set at that first-round effect) that it says are not forecasts and uses only to size the uprating shortfall; they are not pinned, so no inflation figure is staged. The Autumn Budget is on 28 October 2026 (the analysis's config.py), after this search.

producers.note: Staged: Cebr (real-income loss per household and in aggregate, 2026 and 2027) and the TUC's social tariff costings. Price-cap figures are staged where their primary can be read (RF's and HM Treasury's), as energy_bill_change claims: the dashboard sets such figures beside its energy channel in its own comparison table. Cornwall Insight's forecasts, the source JRF cites for £288, could not be read: its press releases and predictions page returned 401 to both a direct fetch and WebFetch. Ofgem's announced caps are administrative outturns (the July 2026 rise of 13.5% anchors the Summer 2026 prices scenario, parameters.registry.low_shock) and are not staged. Seen and not staged: RSM's 2026 real household disposable income scenarios (aggregate macro scenarios); the OECD's April 2026 report (describes UK measures, gives no UK estimate); the End Fuel Poverty Coalition's 8 April 2026 post (prices only; fuel-poverty counts attributed to the Coalition appeared only in search results, and the analysis publishes no fuel poverty figure, metadata.fuel_poverty); Energy UK's March 2026 paper (401, not read).
